scope: The Union defence budget FY2000-01 → FY2026-27 as the Ministry of Defence's demands for grants print it: Defence Services (Revenue) with the Army, Navy, Air Force, Ordnance (OFB, then Directorate of Ordnance) and R&D heads and their Pay & Allowances lines; Capital Outlay on Defence Services with its service totals (where printed) and main categories; Defence Pensions by service; MoD Civil including the Coast Guard, the Border Roads Development Board and Defence Estates — BE, RE and actuals for every FY the fetched documents give (every FY has a BE; actuals for 2009-10, 2012-13, 2014-15, 2016-17, 2018-19, 2020-21, 2022-23, 2024-25). Entities: the ministry, the services, DRDO, IDS, BRO, Coast Guard, DGDE, the pension demand, OFB and its seven successors, the eight listed DPSUs, and the Defence Ministers 2000–2026 as dated roles. Base rates: the four-demand total against GDP and against total Union expenditure, pension and capital shares, and SIPRI's peer set. Three levels of resolution: Union money resolves to the line item; state money resolves to the Police major head per state (and prisons per state from NCRB), with strength and per-capita figures reported: while BPR&D is down; city money does not exist outside Delhi Police, and city strength has no primary while BPR&D is down — cities get the footprint (installations, commissionerate entities with reported: strength) and the void. This file carries only the Union level; it leaves out procurement awards, DPSU order books, pay scales, Agnipath/OROP terms, the cases and the footprint, which sit in sibling files.

entities.label: Ministry of Defence
entities.sub: Union ministry; four demands for grants (MoD Civil, Defence Services Revenue, Capital Outlay, Defence Pensions)
entities.publicRole: The payer for every rupee in this file; the demands it carries are the Union defence budget.
d: Actual 2024-25, four demands summed: ₹636,003.01 crore (revenue 290,964.51; capital 159,768.40; pensions 157,653.65; civil 27,616.45) [documented]
BE 2026-27, four demands summed: ₹784,678.28 crore = 2.00% of projected GDP and 14.7% of total Union expenditure (BE) [documented]

Demand numbers shift by year: Demands 13–19 in 2001-02; 21–28 in 2005-06; 20–27 (one demand per service) 2009-10 to 2015-16; 20–23 (merged) in 2016-17; 19–22 from 2017-18 except 18–21 in 2019-20 to 2021-22; every budgets row names its demand [documented]

UPA-II (BE 2009-10→2013-14): average shares revenue 48.6% / capital 33.8% / pensions 15.6% / MoD civil 2.1%; nominal CAGR of the MoD total 11.0% (GDP at current prices grew 15.3% a year), real CAGR 2.5% deflating by the GNI implicit deflator (Economic Survey 2025-26 Table 1.1). NDA (BE 2014-15→2026-27): average shares revenue 45.3% / capital 26.6% / pensions 23.3% / civil 4.7%; nominal CAGR 8.8% (GDP 10.0%), real CAGR 4.4% over 2014-15→2025-26 (no deflator yet for 2026-27); the first five NDA years alone: nominal 9.1%, real 5.6%. Pay-to-capital (uniformed Pay & Allowances of the three services ÷ Capital Outlay demand, BE): 2000-01 0.71; 2001-02 0.68; 2004-05 0.46; 2005-06 0.47; 2008-09 0.39; 2009-10 0.71; 2010-11 0.67; 2011-12 0.63; 2013-14 0.67; 2014-15 0.71; 2016-17 1.08; 2017-18 1.10; 2018-19 1.10; 2019-20 1.05; 2020-21 1.03; 2021-22 0.87; 2022-23 0.88; 2023-24 0.85; 2024-25 0.85; 2025-26 0.81; 2026-27 0.68. Reading: under both governments the budget grew a little faster than nominal GDP in some years and slower in others, and the pension share rose under both — the step changes are the 2008-09/2009-10 Sixth Pay Commission arrears and OROP (UPA-II and early NDA), the 7th CPC from 2016-17 (NDA), and the RE 2025-26 spectrum-charges line (NDA). The capital share fell under UPA-II and stayed in the high twenties under NDA; the revenue share is the mirror. Neither record is a scandal: both are the arithmetic of a manpower-heavy force paying pensions out of the same envelope. The 2016-17 budget moved Ordnance Factories and R&D (revenue and capital) into the MoD (Misc) demand for one year, which inflates 'civil' and deflates 'revenue' for BE 2015-16/2016-17 in these averages; the four-demand total is unaffected.

narratives.strongestCase: The four-demand ratio to GDP fell from 3.32% (BE 2000-01) to 2.00% (BE 2026-27) and the share of Union expenditure from about 17% (2014-15) to 14.7% (BE 2026-27, PRS); the Standing Committee on Defence (2018) asked for about 3% of GDP; China spends 3.6× India in constant dollars.
narratives.strongestCounter: India is SIPRI's fifth-largest spender; its ratio (2.22% of GDP, SIPRI 2024) sits above the UK's and China's reported ratios, and the Ministry of Finance's position (quoted by PRS) is that allocation follows need and resources, not a fixed share. In rupees the four demands grew 8.8% a year 2014-15→2026-27 against GDP growth of 10.0%; the fall in the ratio is the denominator.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: A costed force-structure requirement (the Standing Committee's projected-vs-allocated tables, or an LTIPP) showing a persistent gap in actuals, not in BE; or a GDP-neutral measure such as spend per serving soldier against peers.

narratives.claim: Pensions are eating the defence budget.
narratives.strongestCase: Defence Pensions rose from 16.9% of the MoD total (BE 2000-01) to a peak of 28.4% (2020-21) and stands at 21.8% in BE 2026-27 (₹171,338 crore), close to the whole Capital Outlay demand (₹219,306 crore); salaries and pensions together are 44% of BE 2026-27 (PRS).
narratives.strongestCounter: The share has fallen back from its 2020-21 peak as Agnipath-era recruitment and the end of OROP arrears slow the growth: pension BE 2026-27 is only +6.6% over BE 2025-26 while capital is +21.8%. Pensions are a contract with people who already served; the 'eating' metaphor treats a liability as a choice.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: A pensioner head-count and average-pension series (DESW) that separates volume from rate; the first Agnipath cohort reaching four years in 2026-27 and the Ministry's stated saving being tested in RE.
srcs: Expenditure Budget 2026-27, Notes on Demands for Grants, Demands 19–22 (Ministry of Defence)

narratives.strongestCase: Capital Outlay's share of the MoD total fell from 37.6% (BE 2004-05) to 33.2% (BE 2014-15) and 27.9% (BE 2026-27); actual 2024-25 (₹159,768 crore) fell ₹12,232 crore short of BE.
narratives.strongestCounter: In rupees the capital demand went from ₹54,824 crore (BE 2009-10) to ₹219,306 crore (BE 2026-27), +17% over RE 2025-26, and in real terms grew 2.2% a year 2014-15→2025-26; actuals exceeded BE in 2016-17 and 2020-21. The share fell because pensions, pay and in 2025-26 spectrum charges grew inside the same envelope.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: A multi-year run of capital actuals below RE with surrendered funds (CAG audit paragraphs on unspent capital), or committed liabilities exceeding the modernisation balance in the Standing Committee tables.

gaps: Actuals for FY2001-02, 2002-03, 2003-04, 2005-06, 2006-07, 2007-08, 2010-11, 2011-12, 2013-14, 2015-16, 2017-18, 2019-20, 2021-22, 2023-24 and RE for 2001-02, 2002-03, 2003-04, 2005-06, 2006-07, 2007-08, 2011-12, 2012-13: they sit in the odd-year Notes on Demands (e.g. indiabudget.gov.in/budget2025-26/doc/eb/sbe20.pdf for actual 2023-24) which the fetch budget did not reach; the Summary of Demands for those years is BE-only (and image-only PDFs for 2013-14 and 2015-16).

Pay & Allowances for BE/RE 2015-16 and actual 2014-15: the 2016-17 document prints them in a second, old-structure block that the extractor did not read; BE 2012-13 pay is absent because only the Summary was fetched for that year.
Government holding in Hindustan Shipyard Ltd and Goa Shipyard Ltd (unlisted; GSL is majority-held by Mazagon Dock) was not verified; the DDP Annual Report 2024-25 states only BEML's 54% in words.

Registered-office states of the seven ex-OFB companies are given from their public identity (MIL Pune, AVNL Chennai, AWEIL/TCL/GIL Kanpur, YIL Nagpur, IOL Dehradun) and were not fetched; the companies' own pages or MCA would confirm.

Ministers' tenure dates come from Wikipedia (reported); mod.gov.in and the Cabinet Secretariat notifications were not reachable; a PIB release on the Cabinet approval of OFB corporatisation (16 Jun 2021) was not located (two guessed PRIDs resolved to unrelated releases and are not cited).

Total Union expenditure for BE 2015-16, 2019-20 to 2024-25 and actuals 2011-12, 2013-14, 2014-15 was not collected (the Budget at a Glance for those years was not fetched), so the %-of-Union-expenditure base rate is missing for those (fy, stage) pairs.
GDP uses the 2011-12 series with the Economic Survey's back-cast for 1996-97→2013-14 and the Budget projection for 2026-27; MoSPI's own press note was not fetched (404 on the guessed path).
The CAPFs that SIPRI adds to India's figure are in the union-home domain, not here; a reconciled all-force ratio needs both files.
